top_stories.title: Stanford Report Highlights Growing Disconnect Between AI Insiders and Everyone Else
top_stories.summary: A new Stanford report reveals a widening gap in perceptions of AI between those working inside the technology industry and the general public. The findings suggest that AI optimism is heavily concentrated among insiders, while broader society holds more cautious or skeptical views.

top_stories.title: The AI Revolution in Math Has Arrived
top_stories.summary: Quanta Magazine reports that AI systems are now making meaningful contributions to mathematical research, marking a significant milestone in the application of AI to formal reasoning and proof-finding. The piece explores how AI tools are being used by mathematicians and what this means for the future of the discipline.

top_stories.title: The Tech Jobs Bust Is Real. Don't Blame AI (Yet)
top_stories.summary: The Economist examines the ongoing contraction in tech employment, arguing that while job losses are real and significant, the evidence does not yet point to AI as the primary cause. The piece considers cyclical and structural factors alongside AI-driven automation.

top_stories.title: How PR Teams Are Using AI Synthetic Focus Groups to Research and Test Messages
top_stories.summary: PR and communications teams are increasingly turning to AI-generated synthetic focus groups to test messaging and creative ideas before launch, replacing or supplementing traditional consumer research methods. The approach raises questions about the reliability and representativeness of AI-simulated audience responses.

top_stories.title: AI Agents Are Coming for Your Dating Life
top_stories.summary: Wired reports on the emerging use of AI agents in online dating, where automated systems are increasingly handling conversations, profile curation, and matchmaking on behalf of users. The trend raises ethical questions about authenticity and consent in romantic contexts.

further_links.title: You Can Soon Buy a $4,370 Humanoid Robot on AliExpress
further_links.summary: Unitree's R1 humanoid robot is set to go on sale via AliExpress, marking a new milestone in consumer-accessible robotics.

further_links.title: AI Influencers Are 'Everywhere' at Coachella
further_links.summary: AI-generated influencers have become a visible presence at Coachella 2026, signalling the growing mainstream integration of synthetic personas in entertainment and marketing.

further_links.title: The Human Cost of 10x: How AI Is Physically Breaking Senior Engineers
further_links.summary: A first-hand account explores how pressure to use AI to dramatically increase productivity is taking a physical and mental toll on senior software engineers.

further_links.title: Celonis Expands Oracle Cloud Tie-Up for Enterprise AI
further_links.summary: Celonis has expanded its partnership with Oracle Cloud, deepening enterprise AI capabilities around process intelligence and automation.

further_links.title: An AI Vibe Coding Horror Story
further_links.summary: A developer shares a cautionary tale about over-relying on AI-assisted 'vibe coding', detailing how it led to serious technical problems and unexpected consequences.

further_links.title: Legal AI Software Market Set for Explosive Growth
further_links.summary: A new market research report forecasts rapid expansion in the legal AI software sector, citing demand from law firms and corporate legal departments.

further_links.title: AI Could Be the End of the Digital Wave, Not the Next Big Thing
further_links.summary: A blog post drawing on Carlota Perez's technology wave theory argues that AI may represent the maturation and end of the digital era rather than the beginning of a new transformative wave.

further_links.title: Physical AI Deployments in Manufacturing and Logistics to Hit 400,000 by 2030
further_links.summary: New research forecasts that physical AI systems, including robots and autonomous equipment, will reach 400,000 deployments across manufacturing and logistics within four years.

further_links.title: GAIA – Open-Source Framework for Building AI Agents That Run on Local Hardware
further_links.summary: GAIA is a newly released open-source framework designed to enable developers to build and run AI agents entirely on local hardware, without reliance on cloud services.
